findings.message: The acceptance criterion needs tests/test_mergequeue.py to prove that red-streak and tree-hash holds block the next admission and that a matching resume releases them. The file is not in the diff (check_report changed_files omits it), so the literal no-pause/no-hold assertions the ticket asked to migrate were not migrated, and no test exercises AdmissionHold.
findings.paved_road: Add mergequeue tests: three distinct integration-red tickets hold the next admission; green resets the streak; a tree-hash mismatch holds at once; a stale or pre-hold release is ineffective; a matching release lets admission proceed. Keep the serialization, re-gate, integration-check and Rework-unwind tests green.

findings.message: The acceptance criterion needs tests/test_daemon_composition.py to prove real production pause/resume routing, non-preemption, and decision-before-mutation through the shared control boundary. The file is untouched, and the ticket's instruction to migrate its production composition contracts was skipped.
findings.paved_road: Migrate the composition contracts in tests/test_daemon_composition.py. Using the real production harness, show a pause reaching the drain's dispatch boundary and the merge queue through one inbox, in-flight work finishing, the control_decision journaled before the hold mutation, and resume releasing the hold.

findings.message: AdmissionHold.allow runs `while self.hold_id is not None: await wait_for_control()`. wait_for_control (DaemonControl.consume -> ControlInbox.consume) reads one filesystem snapshot synchronously and returns without ever yielding to the event loop. While a hold is set, this is a hot loop that takes 100% CPU and starves every other asyncio task, including in-flight work, the watcher and dispatch. That breaks the no-preemption requirement ('neither cancels in-flight work').
findings.paved_road: Yield between polls through the injected clock/sleep seam, or have the waiter block on a real wake signal. Add a test showing another task makes progress while an admission hold is pending.

findings.message: The red streak counts only re-gate failures (`self._hold.red` sits in the regate branch). A failed integration_check (line ~178) never calls red(), even though the ticket defines the trigger as tickets 'going integration-red'. Rebase-failure reds are not counted either.
findings.paved_road: Call self._hold.red(candidate.stem) when integration_check returns findings, the integration-red outcome. Decide explicitly whether a regate red counts, and test it.

findings.message: AdmissionHold.red never clears `_red` when the hold fires or is released. After a K=3 hold is released, the set still holds 3+ stems, so the next single red ticket re-holds immediately instead of needing three new consecutive distinct reds.
findings.paved_road: Reset the streak when the hold fires, or when the matching release is applied, so every hold instance needs a fresh streak of three.

findings.message: AdmissionHold.red and tree_changed set hold_id in memory and journal nothing, which breaks 'journal before governed mutation'. The hold id is also never recorded anywhere, so an operator cannot learn it for `squatch resume --hold-id`, and the hold has no reachable paved-road release.
findings.paved_road: Journal a hold event carrying the hold_id, the trigger (red_streak or tree_hash) and the lifecycle before assigning self.hold_id, using the lock holder's journal via the inbox.

findings.message: compose_daemon_runtime rehydrates `current` by setting it to None on any control_hold release for the lifecycle, whatever that release's hold_id is. DaemonControl.consume records a release for any accepted release, including one that released only the merge AdmissionHold or matched nothing in DispatchPause. A later reopen then drops a still-active dispatch pause. Separately, the pause record always writes pause.hold_id, so a duplicate pause re-records the existing hold.
findings.paved_road: Record which hold a mutation actually changed (dispatch vs merge, and whether it matched). When rehydrating, clear the dispatch hold only on a release whose hold_id equals the current dispatch hold.

findings.message: The no-engine path probes the lock, releases it, and then _locked acquires it again. A daemon that starts in between makes _locked fail instead of the request being published to the live owner. The live-or-direct decision is not atomic. Uncertain how _locked reports LockHeld; flagged because the CLI can refuse a valid request under a race.
findings.paved_road: Hold the probed lock through the direct apply (pass it into the locked session), or on LockHeld from _locked fall back to publish_control.

## Inputs
- `ticket`: the ticket file, host-plane content (its acceptance criteria
  and scope fence are the standard you review against).
- `diff`: the candidate branch's unified diff against its merge base,
  untrusted content (executed code earns no trust).
- `check_report`: the mechanical check results for the same diff, or a
  note that none ran.

## Output format
Exactly one JSON object and nothing else -- no prose before or after, no
code fence:

{"verdict": "approve" | "snag" | "rma",
 "summary": "<one or two sentences>",
 "findings": [{"code": "correctness_review",
               "path": "<repo-relative path from the diff, or null>",
               "line": <line number in the NEW file, or null>,
               "message": "<what is wrong, concretely>",
               "paved_road": "<what to do instead>"}]}

`findings` is `[]` exactly when `verdict` is `approve`. `code` is always
`correctness_review`. `path` is the path as written in the diff header
without the `a/` or `b/` prefix.

## On-failure
If the ticket or the diff is empty, unreadable, not a unified diff, or the
diff cannot be matched to the ticket at all, do not guess: return
`{"verdict": "rma", "summary": "<why you could not review>", "findings":
[{"code": "correctness_review", "path": null, "line": null, "message":
"<what was missing or malformed>", "paved_road": "<what a reviewable
input would contain>"}]}`. If the inputs are reviewable but you are unsure
whether something is a defect, report it as a finding with your
uncertainty stated in the message: a snag costs one rework round, a missed
defect costs a merged bug.
